analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. The changed ranges I could see were the date bump on line 3, the re-slice floor funding text around lines 985-989, a cluster service heartbeat paragraph near line 3532, and later edits not shown in the excerpt. Units 17 and 18 cover head lines 1-836 only, so the cluster heartbeat paragraph and the later ranges (about 5234-5376) were not visible to me. They were not examined.

I found no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or data-exposure controls changed in the visible text. The documented behavior is the Nemotron Super managed slot, logprobs, CBv2 prefix cache, and cluster batching. It matches T-041's existing posture: encrypted SSD checkpoints, authenticated tenant cache scope, and a cache kill switch via DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE or DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. The doc references an optional resident-bank mode (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1) for the Super owner. T-041 says production has no resident-RAM prefix cache tier. This may be pre-existing doc text, and the diff does not show it as newly introduced. A later pass should confirm the code and the threat model agree.

The documented re-slice floor change at lines 985-989 affects availability and grant sizing only. The documented per-model behavior follows the existing authenticated cache scope, and I saw no weakening of tenant isolation.

The cluster health-file paragraph (service-health.json vs part-health.json, DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE) is a local liveness mechanism that I did not see in the provided excerpt. I cannot assess it. If the paired code is in the batch, check whether a local process could forge the heartbeat or spoof PID acceptance.

No findings qualify from the visible evidence, and coverage of the later changed ranges is incomplete.
